stem:
Ahmed is 7 years old and has exercise-induced asthma. He only gets symptoms when playing at school or playing soccer at the weekend. His friends use spacers at school.

Which factor is most important when choosing a rescue medication device for Ahmed to support adherence?

options.text: The device Ahmed is most likely to accept and use correctly
The device that provides the theoretically best drug delivery, regardless of preference
The fact that his friends use spacers

explanation: When choosing a rescue medication device in a child, adherence depends heavily on whether the child will accept the device, can use it correctly, and whether the device fits the child's routine and preferences. Clinical effectiveness is important, but a device that is rejected or used poorly will not work well in practice.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: The original item is about adherence factors rather than asking a factual best option among the provided statements. Rewriting makes it a single-best-answer question with one clearly correct choice about choosing a device that the child will actually use correctly.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Acceptance and correct technique are key determinants of adherence and real-world effectiveness.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Cost matters, but it should not be the sole deciding factor.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. The most effective device on paper may still fail if the child will not use it.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Peer influence may affect acceptance, but it is not the main determinant on its own.
